First Step: download a 'wallet'. -It holds your BTC (Bitcoin).

Why is this awesome? It's your access point to spending BTC. They have very secure front-ends. No PW, no access.

You have a unique set of passwords that will let you recreate your wallet if you lose your old one. (Computer stolen? As long as you have your password login required, they won't crack your wallet). Reinstall wallet software on new computer, enter in your passphrase, it will reload your wallet on the new computer.

How secure is it? No quantum computer=no stolen BTC wallets.

It's free to move money around. Paying for moving BTC is optional, but will speed up your transaction process. (The fee is stupidly small, so people pay the measly .001%)

Here's the cool part: All BTC transaction get recorded on the block chain. It's like a big paper receipt that shows ALL transactions. Whys that cool? It's open accounting. It's UNALTERABLE. This one aspect of BTC is poised to change the future of banking and finance.

Don't worry about getting BTC. As you move around the community. You'll find people dealing in BTC. Then it becomes really easy to accept payments. Oh, and it's pretty much an inventory system in that regards. You can adjust your wallet to show what other wallets are paying you. You can give unique identifiers from your wallet and make sub-addresses if it suits you, and you can make as many as you want and you can add notes to your transactions. It's flexible and useful and makes a lot of otherwise difficult tasks very easy.

Spending BTC? Becoming easier everyday. Amazon, tiger-direct, overstock, etc.

Whys BTC better than money? There's a hundred reasons. My favorite is they can't devalue BTC by printing more. It's also an international currency at this point.
